The real case is better than the caricature. No early Christian kept birthdays. Origen wrote that only sinners, such as Pharaoh and Herod, mark the day of their birth. So the Witness reading has early-church backing. Cakes, candles and wishes do come down from pagan charms, per standard reference works. Nobody is harmed by sitting one out. Christmas rests on a date and customs that are not Christian, and on a nativity timeline many non-Witness scholars doubt. Standing apart honours a conscience aimed at pure worship (2 Corinthians 6:17).

Not in standing apart. In being made to. Paul leaves days to each person. Romans 14:5-6 says it plainly: "let each one be fully convinced in his own mind." One man rates one day above another. Another rates every day alike. See also Colossians 2:16. Watchtower policy treats a birthday as proof that you have left, with family shunning downstream. Note also that the movement kept Christmas until 1928, and birthdays until about 1951.
Genuinely arguable, both ways. Sitting these out is a fair use of liberty, and it has early-church backing. Mocking it plays badly. Aim only at the force, never at the quiet conscience.
"I have no problem with you skipping birthdays. My question is why Romans 14:5 does not make it your own call."

higher-education-discouraged.d: For decades, university has been described as a spiritual danger. The Watchtower of October 1, 2005 (pp. 26-31) urged young ones toward theocratic goals instead. Governing Body member Anthony Morris III gave a broadcast in May 2017 called "What Is the Best Education?", urging Bethel service over degrees. In 2023 Stephen Lett compared sending a child to university to a school of hungry sharks. Circuit overseers have been directed that an elder whose family pursue higher education may lose his appointment.

higher-education-discouraged.t: What it has cost, in numbers
higher-education-discouraged.d: Pew Research measured it. About 9% of US Jehovah's Witnesses hold a bachelor's degree. That is the lowest of any major US religious group surveyed, against a national average of about 35%. Household incomes track it.

Their own senior counsel, Philip Brumley, holds a law degree. Bethel keeps qualified lawyers, doctors and engineers on hand. Those are exactly the skills the counsel would have kept members from getting.

They have never banned education. They require literacy and teach millions to read, and they leave schooling to families. Their counsel weighs real data that secular writers also raise: student debt, campus culture, graduates in jobs that do not need degrees. Vocational training has been encouraged for years. And the priority is spiritual. If the Kingdom is real, seeking it first (Matthew 6:33) is rational, and warning against careerism is what any serious faith does.

They admit this themselves. The counsel is in their own broadcasts and magazines, and the outcome is measured by neutral survey data. A 2025 Governing Body update reframed education as a personal choice. That is genuine, and it arrived after the generations who obeyed had paid for it. Scripture never treats learning as apostasy. Moses was schooled in all Egypt's wisdom (Acts 7:22). Paul studied under Gamaliel (Acts 22:3). "The plans of the diligent one surely make for advantage" (Proverbs 21:5).
"Moses was trained in all the wisdom of Egypt and Paul studied under Gamaliel. What changed?"

avoid-no-medical-treatment.d: That Jehovah's Witnesses reject medicine, like the extreme faith-healing groups. It is false, and it is easy for them to disprove.

Almost all of it. Surgery. Medication. Chemotherapy. Vaccines, encouraged since 1952. Organ transplants, permitted since 1980. Intensive care. The one standing ban is whole blood and its four primary parts.

The organization runs Hospital Information Services and roughly 1,700 Hospital Liaison Committees, in more than 110 countries. They connect members with bloodless medicine and willing surgical teams. That effort has genuinely advanced techniques that avoid transfusion, and those techniques now help patients who are not Witnesses at all.

avoid-no-medical-treatment.t: Why the false version costs you
avoid-no-medical-treatment.d: It hands a Witness an easy and honest correction. Worse, it discredits the accurate criticisms standing beside it: the 1945 origin of the blood ban, the fractions line that does not hold, and the children celebrated in 1994.
Do not use this one. Keep the criticism precise. The issue is one lethal ban with a shifting boundary. It is not hostility to medicine.
"I know you take medicine and surgery. My question is only about blood, and about where the line moved."

avoid-jws-worship-russell.d: That Jehovah's Witnesses revere or follow Charles Taze Russell as a man. It comes out of anti-cult books written a long time ago.

Today they do not worship Russell, and few of them read him. The Society dropped much of what he taught. It dropped his pyramid teaching. It dropped the details of his dates. It dropped his view of the higher powers. It took a new name in 1931, partly to shed the Russellite label. His books are not in print, and not in use.
Call them Russellites and any Witness can place your source. It was written before they were born. It tells them you have not looked at the faith as it is now.

There is a fair version of this. They grant the Governing Body a power much like the one they attack in other churches. Make that point straight. Use the sole-channel material, and what Geoffrey Jackson said on oath.
Do not use this one. Use Russell only for what he wrote. He taught that the body of Jesus may have been turned to gas. That is a real quote. So is his line that Jesus was rightly worshipped.
"I'm not interested in Russell as a person. I'm interested in who has authority now, and where that authority comes from."

avoid-2024-shunning-ended.d: Since March 2024 people have said that Jehovah's Witnesses abolished shunning. They did not.

Governing Body Update #2 of March 2024, given by Mark Sanderson, and the August 2024 Watchtower set it out. Members may now offer a simple greeting to a removed person, and invite them to meetings. Elders may make shepherding visits and study the Bible with them. Judicial steps and reinstatement were streamlined. Minors are handled with a parent present. And "disfellowshipping" became "removal from the congregation."

Expulsion itself. The announcement. The direction against normal social contact. Treating a formal resignation the same as being thrown out. And the loss of normal family life with relatives outside the household. Ex-member groups and mainstream coverage agree the core stands.
It lets a Witness correct you truthfully. It also concedes, without meaning to, that the softer version is good enough.

Do not use this one. Use the accurate version, which is stronger. What was compulsory cruelty in 2023, refusing even a hello, became optional kindness in 2024. No new verse was discovered in between. That tells you the old severity was policy, not divine law.
"In 2023 you could not say hello. In 2024 you can. Which Bible verse changed?"

avoid-dismiss-persecution-record.d: "They're just a cult, there's nothing to respect about them." It usually comes out as a warm-up to a point about 1914 or blood. It is not only rude. It is false, and the Witness in front of you knows the history far better than you do.

avoid-dismiss-persecution-record.t: What they did under the Third Reich
avoid-dismiss-persecution-record.d: They were the one group held for a belief they could drop at any moment. A signature on a form would have freed them. Roughly 10,000 were jailed. Around 1,500 died. About 250 were put to death for refusing to serve in the army. They wore the purple triangle in the camps. Survivors, Jewish survivors among them, describe them as the least likely to inform and the most likely to share food.

avoid-dismiss-persecution-record.t: What they won in American courts
avoid-dismiss-persecution-record.d: Between 1938 and 1955 they took more than fifty cases to the Supreme Court. What they won belongs to everyone. West Virginia v. Barnette (1943) held that no American can be made to salute a flag, or to state a belief. Cantwell v. Connecticut (1940) applied the free exercise of faith to the states. Much of the religious freedom every US church leans on was bought by Jehovah's Witnesses in court.
Russia banned them as extremist in 2017. Members have been jailed there ever since.

A Witness has heard this story since childhood. It is part of how the group proves to members that opposition means truth. Say it yourself, first, and mean it. Then that defense has nowhere to go. Then note the line that does the work. Willingness to suffer proves sincerity. Nobody disputes their sincerity. It does not prove the doctrine, and the doctrine is the question. Every martyr in history was sincere. The Beroeans were praised for checking the message anyway (Acts 17:11).
"Before anything else: what your people did under Hitler, and what you won at the Supreme Court, I respect completely."
